objects_built.name: require_manager
objects_built.role: Reads the given user's row and stops the call with accessdenied unless role is manager. Called by the refund-approve and price-change endpoints.

objects_changed.name: refunds/{refund_id}/approve
objects_changed.change: Added function.run require_manager with user_id = $auth.id before the db.edit refunds.

objects_changed.name: products/{product_id}/price
objects_changed.change: Added function.run require_manager with user_id = $auth.id before the db.patch products.

objects_changed.name: me
objects_changed.change: Removed the text role input. Replaced data = $input[""] (whole-body write) with explicit name, phone and marketing_opt_in, closing the self-promotion path.

templates_considered: AUTH-030 no_self_promotion: fits the self-promotion part exactly; used as-is with fields [role].

AUTH-002 admin_endpoints_check_role: template is about admin endpoints; the ask is about manager-only actions. Kept its key and its object.statement_required shape, with functions [require_manager] and the scope on refunds and products. Title changed to match.
AUTH-003 public_endpoints_harmless: no fit; the ask is not about public endpoints.
AUTH-050, AUTH-040, BIZ-001: no fit for this ask, or only loosely (BIZ-001 is check-before-write ordering, which statement_order would need per-table functions for; not used).
RET-001 / audit recipes: out of scope for this ask.

rules.covers: Refund edits (approval) only happen after the manager check.
Same, for patch writes to refunds.
Price changes (edit) only after the manager check.
Price changes (patch) only after the manager check; this is the one the price endpoint uses.
Nobody can set their own role from request input; me PATCH no longer takes it.

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Regular staff can view but not change: all changes other than refunds and prices (customer edits, payments, bank links, etc.)
Only managers may approve refunds or change prices, for writes that do not use db.edit or db.patch on refunds/products (db.add_or_edit, db.bulk.*, db.direct_query, etc.)
Nobody can just give themselves manager, via internal or admin tooling that writes role from a fixed value
Who is allowed to be a manager (who gets the role, who approves it)

assumptions: "Change prices" means the products/{product_id}/price PATCH endpoint, and "approve refunds" means refunds/{refund_id}/approve POST.
"Manager" is the users.role value "manager"; admin is not included because the ask says only managers.
"Regular staff" is the users.role value "staff"; the restriction is implemented as 'not manager', which also covers member and viewer.
Customer approved a plan and wants it built in one change; policies are active and advisory, not blocking, per the skill's rule for new policies.
confusions: AUTH-002's template and check description are about admin endpoints; there is no template for 'role-restricted action', so I reused AUTH-002 with a manager function and scoped rules. Unclear whether a template can be re-scoped this way or should get its own key.

The skill says a rule with a tables scope is judged by reaching objects; whether when.statement + when.tables matches db.patch inside a function called from an endpoint is not stated. I scoped to endpoint stacks by reasoning only.
Catalogue/skill do not say whether a new object should carry a guid line; the existing workspace files all do. I left it off the two new/edited files that had none to copy (the new function).
The brief says policies go in ./workspace/policies/, the skill says /policies/ relative to the project root; I followed the brief.
wished_for: A way to say 'write of this table only via this function' that fits a per-field, per-statement case without a restricted-tables policy (table.write_location_restricted would need the endpoints rewritten to call a single writer function).
An example of a role-restricted policy (manager-only actions) with the function signature the check expects (e.g. does it need $auth or an id input).
A note on whether object.statement_required sees function.run calls that themselves do the write, to know if the scope is judged on the caller's stack or the callee's.
dry_run_problems_seen: Dry run exit 0; no policy findings printed (dry-run does not evaluate policies, and I did not run xano policy evaluate, which the brief forbids). Parse warned that require_manager is not on the branch: expected, since it is part of this change.
why_confidence: The refund-approve and price endpoints now call a manager-only function, and AUTH-002 checks that. Self-promotion through me PATCH is removed and AUTH-030 checks for role from input. Confidence is not high because the rules only see db.edit and db.patch on two tables, the regular-staff restriction covers only refunds and prices, and nothing has been evaluated against the live branch, so the findings are predictions.
